column5: The three recorded volume-capacity values are arithmetically averaged at each source temperature. Following the primary reduction, temperatures are rounded to 0.1 degC, giving 10,20,30,40 degC; Celsius-to-Kelvin adds exactly 273.15. Computed replicate sample standard deviation is sqrt(sum((C_i-mean_C)^2)/(3-1)), retained as a separate TabulatedOnly statistic rather than a confidence interval or instrument uncertainty. Extra decimal places in computed means/standard deviations are arithmetic, not additional measurement resolution. Linear interpolation of the mean C(T) and reported Cp(T) is an authored approximation between these four source temperature groups, with no extrapolation or quantified interpolation error. FSRI uses the mean of the reported rounded density column, 51.666666666666664 kg/m3, for heat-capacity normalization; recomputing mass/volume would change that published reduction. Density measurement temperature is unspecified. The reference-normalization-density value is an arithmetic normalization input with no temperature validity, not a constant density law or bulk-density measurement at every thermal knot.

FSRI divides mean native volumetric heat capacity by the common mean reported density, then rounds to whole J/(kg K): 1332,1360,1417,1465 at 10,20,30,40 degC. Reported standard deviations 12,13,20,16 J/(kg K) divide native volume-capacity sample SD by that same mean density, rounded to whole units. They do not propagate density scatter or calibration uncertainty. Cp, C and normalization density are algebraically related; they are not three independent measurements. Rounded published Cp is retained without replacing it with an unrounded ratio.
